# Project State

_Last updated: 2026-10-11_

## Current phase

**Phase 2 — End-to-end demo built (2026-10-10).** Atahan delegated the whole challenge to the agent ("full power, sole competitor").
- Evidence layer complete: 10,128 verbatims (extract-v3, D-024), customer study (391 items), sales, option lists (458 items), reference layer (96 cited sources), web research (219 cited items, 152 web findings).
- Findings: verbatim clusters G60 243 · F70 166 · G70 242 (D-025), 391 study findings (D-026).
- Requirements pipeline: derivation (sol, derive-v6) → portfolio consolidation → dedup vs backlog (D-035) → evidence linker → fit checks → scoring v3 → change proposals, orchestrated per simulated wave (LangGraph, D-027–D-029). D-038: defects go to a Quality hand-over page instead of becoming requirements, strict merging, markets without comments can't outrank evidenced ones, one priority for Expected needs.
- PM app (Streamlit, D-032, restructured D-036, D-037: Home → How it works → Review → Priorities by market → AI suggestions, plus detail pages, Quality hand-over (D-038) and a demo tour) with approve/reject/defer/edit/challenge/override/priority/inbox, audit trail, export.
- Demo states via `scripts/demo_state.py` + `scripts/demo_build.py` (snapshots `evidence`, `wave1`, `demo`).

## Team & logistics (fill in — Q-007, Q-008)

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Team members & roles | _TODO_ |
| Who plays the PM in the demo | _TODO_ |
| Submission deadline | _TODO_ |
| Demo format / length | _TODO_ |
| Judging criteria (beyond the brief) | _TODO_ |

## Minimal demo path (decided, D-021)

One thin slice end-to-end before anything else (AGENTS rule 18). It covers BMW's minimum of one derivative in one market (`challenge-brief.md`).
- **Scope:** 5 Series (D-005).
  - **G60 × US:** ~3.6k verbatims + detailed study + sales. Best-evidenced.
  - **G68 × CN:** study + sales, no verbatims, so web evidence and the market conflict carry it (D-011).
  - G60 × EU as an optional third target (~110 verbatims + study).
- **Flow:**
  1. Classify the G60 verbatims.
  2. Group them into findings with sources.
  3. Derive ~10–15 requirements with targets US/CN.
  4. Run fit checks.
  5. Score and explain.
  6. PM approves, rejects or challenges a few.
  7. Show the audit trail.
  8. Run wave 2 (Q-012) and show priority changes + change proposals.
- F70/G70 stay supported by the data model and run later through the same pipeline.

## Done

- Challenge analyzed; all BMW data profiled and re-verified (`documents/data-inventory.md`).
- Foundation, `AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md` created.
- BMW mentor input recorded (D-011 markets differ, D-012 future needs, D-013 continuous re-prioritization). BMW support recommended the annual report → `documents/bmw-annual-report-2025.md`.
- Model tiering (D-010); budget re-baselined (D-014).
- Q-001/002/003 answered by Atahan → D-005 (portfolio-level, 5 Series deepest), D-006 (OpenAI), D-007 (web knowledge base), D-008 (brand fit gate), D-009 (plant/platform feasibility).
- Conceptual architecture, requirement model and knowledge-base design drafted. Tech stack decided 2026-10-10 (D-015–D-020).
- Web research seeds written and fact-checked:
  - `portfolio-reference.md`: platforms, 14 vehicle plants + 3 CKD sites, BMW sales 2024–H1 2026, primary-sourced from the annual report where possible.
  - `competitor-landscape.md`: competitors, trends, expectations, brand-fit guardrails.
- Foundation review (2026-10-10) fixed, except the confidentiality items, which Atahan dropped.

## In progress

- **Requirement definition layer (D-048, page 3 `/definition`)** — contract `documents/requirement-definition.md`. Done: `definition/domains.py` (domains, aspect→zone, aspect→resources; zone `underfloor`), `benchmarks.py` (246 cited `spec_fact` rows, 210 visible; gap research 26 web items), `define` cp1 (run 20: 76 requirements from 36 areas), `couple` cp1 (run 24: 73 links — 0 conflicts, attention-heavy; judge fix requested for cp2), API `/api/definition`, page 3 (car, pins by domain, link arcs, ladder inspector + PM choice, 4-stage stepper (Drafted → Specified → Linked → On the car) where the page-2 diamonds rise and, still rising, burst into requirements before landing on the car, Agent panel for define/specify/couple). **Running:** `specify` cp1 re-run (run 25) — run 23 had 249/252 thresholds as gaps and rating-share metrics, re-prompted to use benchmark attributes and competitor-feature thresholds; then cp2 define → specify → couple with carry-forward. Ceiling $4.00 for the layer. Open for Atahan: page-read dates for 4 web items, and whether undated OEM spec pages may count as "current at retrieval" (12 items invisible under D-041).
- Rebuild on two real-date checkpoints (D-040, D-041). Done: research layer (1,028 cited items incl. China round 2), checkpoint lineage in the DB (`checkpoint_run` / `track`, stage `acquire` at cp1 and cp2), comment galaxy, new frontend with the Scan screen (`uv run python -m api` + `cd web && npm run dev` → http://127.0.0.1:5173). **Waiting for Atahan** to lead classification → clustering → contextualization → requirement elicitation; each will be a stage on the checkpoint API.

## Demo (how to run)

- **New PM app (D-039):** `uv run python -m api` → http://127.0.0.1:8600 (serves the built app from `web/dist`; build once with `cd web && npm install && npm run build`). Dev mode: API + `cd web && npm run dev` → http://127.0.0.1:5173.
- **Pitch:** click **Present** in the top band (or ⌘K → "Present the demo story"): Briefing → Decide (AI priority change, then one requirement decided with a reason) → 5 Series USA in 3D → 5 Series LWB China (cockpit x-ray) → Markets/China → REQ-0001 fully opened ("Trace step by step") → Evidence gaps → Process timeline → Audit → Deliverable. `[` / `]` step.
- **3D models:** `data/models/{f70,g60,g70}.glb` (git-ignored, Q-025); without them a placeholder car renders.
- DB holds the full `demo` state (wave 3). To replay waves live: Process → System → restore `wave1` (or `uv run python scripts/demo_state.py restore wave1` with the API stopped).
- Legacy Streamlit app: `uv run streamlit run app.py` (to be retired).

## Next up (suggested order)

- **Open after the 2026-10-11 structure run (D-043):** (1) session "ed" is running D-047 relink cp1 → cp2 + D-046 market backfill — then check /structure in a real browser at JAN and JUL (morph, halos, area diamonds, arcs, inspectors); (2) add page-2 sections to DESIGN.md (Structure layer, Funnel, Agent panel, Area/Cluster/Theme inspectors); (3) contextualize themes now use complete linkage 0.35 (71 themes cp1 / 107 cp2) and z-gated theme tracks — note this in D-043 if not yet there; (4) next pipeline step = requirement drafting from areas (`structure/elicit.py` exists, not run); (5) commit the remaining uncommitted work when Atahan asks.


- Validation (2026-10-10, `documents/validation-report.md`): duplicates fixed (D-035); Q-021 and Q-023 closed by D-038, leftovers in Q-024; thin future orientation (42/53 `today`).

0. Fill in Team & logistics (Q-007, Q-008); rehearse the demo path above.
1. Ask BMW mentors: Q-005, Q-006, Q-015, Q-016 (Q-010 is now decided as non-blocking, D-030 — confirm).
2. PM sign-off of the proposed brand guardrails (D-031) — they gate approval.
3. Quality levers (benchmarks in `data/eval/`): judge "measurable" (3.5) and "evidence-grounded" (3.6) are the weakest dimensions; top-20 pain coverage 65–75% after wave 1 (rest picked up in waves 2/3).
4. Optional: async/background wave runs in the UI (currently blocking), wave-3 derivation cap (it still adds ~11 requirements).

## Budget (OpenAI, $100 total — plan in D-014)

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Spent to date | **$10.95** (2026-10-11 10:05: +$2.67 requirement definition D-048 so far — define cp1 $0.90 incl. failed reservations, specify cp1 runs 22/23/25 ≈ $1.0, benchmarks extraction $0.02 + gap research $0.39, couple cp1; +$0.12 D-047 relink cp1+cp2 + embeddings; failed calls hold ≈ $0.35 worst-case reservations, not billed tokens) — was **$8.22** (+$0.84 structure & context pipeline D-043: classify $0.57 incl. A/B + both checkpoints + source mapping, areas $0.19, contextualize $0.08, embeddings $0.01; +$0.009 comment galaxy D-041) — was $7.37 (2026-10-10; +$0.06 validation, +$0.45 dedup demo rebuild D-035): derivation $2.38 (incl. prompt iterations v2–v6, 4 wave-1 runs, waves 2–3 ×2), web research $1.69, fit checks $0.55, extraction $0.52, linker $0.23, recheck $0.13, benchmarks $0.09, challenge $0.08, consolidation $0.08, other $0.12, **plus a $1.00 reconciliation row** (usage rows lost in a failed demo restore, upper-bound estimate; bug fixed). Source of truth: `llm_usage` / Budget page |
| Planned build spend | ≈ $60 (≈ $48 + 25% contingency) |
| Warn / block non-demo / app hard stop | $45 / $70 / $90 |
| Demo-day reserve | $20 ($70 → $90) |
| OpenAI project hard limit | $95 (to set by Atahan, + $45 alert) |

## Pilot results (2026-10-10, `scripts/pilot.py`, outputs in `data/pilot/`)

| Step | Calls | Tokens in / out (reasoning) | Cost | Latency (Flex) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Extract 50 G60 US verbatims (B 20, A/C/D 10 each, seed 42), luna low | 2 × 25 | 3.0k / 3.2k (452); 2.3k / 2.6k (142) | $0.0018 | 84 s, 66 s |
| Derive 5 requirements from 73 signals, sol medium | 1 | 6.1k / 2.1k (279) | $0.0183 | 35 s |

- **Extraction:** every ID returned, none invented, none duplicated; 73 signals; 1 verbatim correctly out of scope ("Nothng."). 1 of 73 quotes not an exact substring (model inserted "he"). Feedback type overlaps BMW's label on 28/39 labelled verbatims; most of the 11 mismatches are BMW "Difficult to Use" on things that are actually faults (CarPlay drops, trunk opening by itself), where our label looks more accurate. Real errors: "seats less comfortable than expected" → `defect`, trunk opening → category Interior. BMW's own label was wrong on G60-0877 (says trunk light, text is about vanity mirror).
- **Derivation:** 5 requirements, every cited ID exists, all have evidence (2–9 verbatims each); spot-checked citations support the claims. Weak points: all 5 tagged `at_successor_launch`, 4/5 Kano `basic`; metrics have no numeric targets (model says so in assumptions); 2 requirements rest on 2–3 verbatims, expected at n=50.
- **Re-estimate (D-014):** extraction ≈ $0.0009 per 25-verbatim call → ≈ $0.36 per full 10.1k run, ≈ $1.1 for 3 runs (plan $1.4). Derivation output was ~420 tokens/requirement vs 6k planned, but real input depends on the findings step (not built), so the derivation estimate stays as is. Plan total unchanged at ≈ $60.
- Prompt caching wrote almost the whole prompt on every call (+25% input, ~8% of pilot cost) with no reuse → Q-018.
- Follow-ups → Q-018. Source D finding → Q-005, `data-inventory.md`.

## G60 extraction results (2026-10-10, extract-v2, `bmw_req.pipeline.run_extract`)

- 160 luna Flex calls (2 validation + 158 full), 16 workers, 12 min; **$0.1348** ($0.00084/call); 421k in / 455k out (58k reasoning); 0 cache writes; 0 failed, 0 missing, 0 invented IDs; no retries needed.
- 4,000 verbatims → 3,732 in scope → **5,400 signals** (US 4,607 · RoW 485 · EU 308).
- Feedback types: like 2,777 · complaint 851 · want 699 · defect 580 · difficult_to_use 493.
- Top categories: Infotainment & Digital 1,023 · Driving Experience 901 · Comfort & Space 781 · Interior 572 · Exterior 550.
- 33 signals (0.6%) have unverified quotes — mostly stitched with "…" or a changed word form ("enjoy" vs "enjoys"); flagged, not dropped.
- Out-of-scope verdicts drop some usable content → Q-019 → re-check below.

## Q-019 re-check results (2026-10-10, `bmw_req.pipeline.recheck`, sol low, Flex)

- 11 calls, **$0.1342** (agent had estimated ≈ $0.05 — off by 2.7×: sol output 1.2–2k tokens/call at $5/M Flex). Avg 3.4k in / 1.6k out per call.
- First attempt: 7 of 11 batches refused by the run's own $0.30 cap, because the cap counts open reservations and each sol call reserves ≈ $0.13 worst case (4 in flight ≈ $0.53). No API calls were made for them; re-run with a $1 cap finished them. Lesson: size run caps to workers × worst-case reservation.
- **111 of 268 flipped to in scope, 157 confirmed out of scope; 118 new signals**, 0 unverified quotes, 0 missing IDs.
- New signals: difficult_to_use 80 (66 of them hotline questions like "customer asked which regen setting to use"), like 17, defect 12, complaint 5, want 4. Real recoveries include "only fast charged to 80%, which i really hated", a flat-tire defect, oil-dipstick want, removed gesture control. The question-type ones are a looser rule than the first pass applied → Q-020.
- G60 now: 3,843 in-scope verbatims, **5,518 signals**.
- Re-estimate: extraction for all 10.1k verbatims ≈ $0.34/run, below D-014's $0.47/run.

# BMW Requirements Studio

AI-assisted, evidence-linked **customer requirements for BMW successor vehicles** — built for the BMW
"AI for Product Decision Making" hackathon challenge. The AI ingests BMW customer feedback, customer studies,
sales and option lists, enriches them with cited web research, extracts signals, clusters findings, derives and
scores requirements per derivative × market — and the **product manager decides**, with every step in an
append-only audit trail.

Portfolio-level from day one: 1 Series (F70), 5 Series (G60 + China LWB G68), 7 Series (G70) × EU / US / CN / RoW.

## Quick start

```bash
uv sync                                   # Python 3.12 venv
cp .env.example .env                      # add OPENAI_API_KEY (LLM provider: OpenAI)
uv run python -m api                      # API on http://127.0.0.1:8600 (serves web/dist when built)
cd web && npm install && npm run dev      # PM app (dev) on http://127.0.0.1:5173
cd web && npm run build                   # then the API alone serves the app at http://127.0.0.1:8600
uv run streamlit run app.py               # legacy Streamlit app (being retired, D-039)
```

The raw BMW data (`challange information document/`) and the database (`data/app.db`) are git-ignored.
Demo states (`data/snapshots/`):

| Snapshot | Contents | Use |
|---|---|---|
| `evidence` | all evidence ingested, no requirements | rebuild the pipeline |
| `wave1` | wave 1 done, no PM decisions | **live demo**: review as the PM from scratch |
| `demo` | wave 1 → PM review → wave 2 → PM decides proposals → wave 3 | explore the full ~2-year history |

```bash
uv run python scripts/demo_state.py restore wave1   # stop the app first; keeps the LLM usage log + cache
uv run python scripts/demo_build.py                 # rebuild wave1 + demo from the evidence snapshot
```

## End-to-end workflow

| # | Step | Who | Where |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Ingest feedback (10,128 verbatims), customer study, sales, option lists | AI/system, autonomous | `bmw_req.ingest` |
| 2 | Curated reference layer (platforms, plants, competitors, market profiles, brand guardrails) | AI-researched, **PM signs off guardrails** | `bmw_req.reference_data` |
| 3 | Web research agents → cited evidence (URL in search citations, quote verified) | AI, autonomous | `bmw_req.research` |
| 4 | Signal extraction (luna) → findings (embeddings + clustering, per-market/per-wave metrics) | AI, autonomous | `pipeline.extract`, `pipeline.findings` |
| 5 | Requirement derivation (sol), portfolio consolidation, dedup against the existing backlog (merge proposals), evidence linking | AI **proposes** | `pipeline.requirements`, `pipeline.linker` |
| 6 | Fit checks: brand (gate), segment, market, feasibility (context) | AI checks, sol re-checks warn/fail | `pipeline.fit` |
| 7 | Explainable per-target scoring, snapshots, change proposals | AI computes, **PM sets weights** | `pipeline.scoring` |
| 8 | Review: approve / reject / defer / edit / challenge / override gate / confirm priority | **Human, mandatory** | PM app |
| 9 | Audit trail, export | system | PM app → Audit trail / Export |

Repeated per **simulated ingest wave** (LangGraph orchestrator `pipeline.graph`): wave 1 kick-off, wave 2
(+6 months: more feedback, customer study, new sales), wave 3 (+12 months: market event from web research).
Scores are recomputed automatically; priority changes against a PM-confirmed priority become **change
proposals** with their factor-level cause.

## How the deliverables map

| BMW deliverable | Where |
|---|---|
| Concept + working prototype | this repo; PM app: Home → How it works → Review requirements → Priorities by market → AI suggestions (sidebar "Demo tour" walks the path) |
| Structured requirement list (ID, description, findings+sources, score, rationale, evidence level, assumptions/uncertainties, status) | Export page (JSON / CSV / Markdown), `service.export_requirements` |
| Workflow definition: AI autonomous vs mandatory human review | table above; Home ("How it works") and Pipeline & data pages; `foundation/documents/architecture.md` |
| Audit trail: sources → findings → consolidation → scoring → prioritization → human decision | Requirement → Audit tab; Audit trail page; `audit_event` (append-only via triggers) |

## Key design choices

- **Evidence vs assumption** kept apart in every requirement; conflicting evidence linked as `contradicts`.
- **Markets are different customers** — every derivative × market target has its own score, evidence level and
  priority; missing data (e.g. no China verbatims) is shown as an evidence gap, not silently scored as zero.
- **Brand fit** is an approval gate (PM override with rationale); **feasibility** is non-blocking context.
- **$100 OpenAI budget** enforced by a reserving wrapper; every call logged in `llm_usage`, identical calls cached.

Project memory, decisions (D-001 … ) and open questions live in `foundation/`.

# Foundation — start here every session

This folder is the project's memory. Every agent (Claude, Codex, humans) reads it at session start and keeps it current.

## Read order (session start)

1. `STATE.md` — where we are, team, demo path, what's next, budget.
2. `OPEN_QUESTIONS.md` — the "Open" section; check if any question blocks your task.
3. `DECISIONS.md` — the **Index** table; open full entries only when relevant (don't re-litigate without new info).
4. Only the `documents/` your task needs (see the table in `AGENTS.md`).

## Write rules (session end / after meaningful work)

- `STATE.md`: update "Current phase", "In progress", "Next up", the Budget table after paid runs, and add one line to the "Session log".
- `DECISIONS.md`: append a new `D-xxx` entry for every decision (who decided, why, alternatives) **and add it to the Index**. Statuses: `accepted` · `proposed` · `superseded by D-xxx`.
- `OPEN_QUESTIONS.md`: add new `Q-xxx` entries in numeric order. When answered, move them to "Resolved" with the answer and link the resulting decision.
- `documents/`: keep reference docs true to the code. If you change the stack, schema or workflow, update the doc in the same change. State each fact **once**: other docs link to it instead of copying it.
- Never present something as decided unless a `D-xxx` says so. Changing the stack (D-015–D-020) needs the team.

## Folder map

| File | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `STATE.md` | Live project status, team, demo path, budget, session log |
| `DECISIONS.md` | Append-only decision log (`D-xxx`) with index |
| `OPEN_QUESTIONS.md` | Open / resolved questions (`Q-xxx`) |
| `documents/challenge-brief.md` | BMW challenge distilled: mission, scope (+ tensions), deliverables, judging signals, mentor input |
| `documents/data-inventory.md` | Every provided dataset: schema, verified counts, quirks, coverage |
| `documents/tech-stack.md` | Decided stack, budget guard as built, what's still open |
| `documents/architecture.md` | End-to-end workflow, AI vs. human steps, logical data model, audit trail |
| `documents/requirement-model.md` | Requirement schema, evidence levels, gates, prioritization draft |
| `documents/knowledge-base.md` | 3-layer knowledge base, research agents, trust tiers, brand fit & feasibility |
| `documents/portfolio-reference.md` | Platforms, plants, production, BMW sales (cited) |
| `documents/competitor-landscape.md` | Competitors per segment × market, demand trends, brand positioning (cited) |
| `documents/bmw-annual-report-2025.md` | BMW Group Report 2025 extract (T1, page-cited) |
| `documents/glossary.md` | Codes, platforms, data and model terms |

## Fresh clone

1. **Raw data** (not in git): put the BMW challenge folder at the repo root under its original name `challange information document/` (typo intended), containing `mission.md`, `BMW_Hackathon_Briefing_Short.pdf`, the three PNGs and `BMW-Data/` (3 feedback xlsx, customer studies xlsx, `sales_volumes.xlsx`, 3 option-list PDFs). Get it from the team. Treat it as read-only.
2. **Python**: `uv sync` (creates `.venv` with Python 3.12 from `pyproject.toml`). Tests: `uv run pytest`. UI: `uv run python -m api` + `cd web && npm install && npm run dev` (D-039; legacy: `uv run streamlit run app.py`). Don't use the system anaconda Python (broken pandas).
3. **PDF tools**: `brew install poppler` for `pdftotext` (option lists) and `pdftoppm`. The briefing PDF has no text layer, so render it with `pdftoppm` to read it.
4. **Secrets**: copy `.env.example` to `.env`, then add `OPENAI_API_KEY` (ask Atahan).
5. **Derived data** and the SQLite DB go to `data/` (git-ignored).

They show the same thing because it's the same app. Both run the code in `frontend/src`; they just deliver it differently.

| | **http://127.0.0.1:8600** | **http://127.0.0.1:5173** |
|---|---|---|
| Who serves the page | The Python API (FastAPI) | Vite, the Node development server |
| What it serves | The built copy in `frontend/dist` (`make build`) | The source files in `frontend/src`, compiled as the browser asks for them |
| When you edit frontend code | Nothing changes until you run `make build` again | The page updates within about a second |
| Where the data comes from | Its own `/api` | It forwards `/api` calls to port 8600 |
| Speed | Faster (minified, a few bundled files) | Slower first load (many unbundled modules) |
| What it needs | Only Python | Node and `npm`, plus the API running |

Right now they match exactly because I ran `make build` during the restructure, so the built copy is up to date with the source. As soon as someone edits a file in `frontend/src`, 5173 shows the change and 8600 keeps showing the old build.

Data and actions are shared: 5173 has no backend of its own, so a decision you make in either tab shows up in the other.

**Which to use:**
- **While changing the frontend:** use 5173.
- **For the demo or pitch:** use 8600. It's one process, faster and won't change mid-presentation. Run `make build` first so it has the latest code.

If you're not editing frontend code right now, you only need 8600, and I can stop the dev server.
why are we running both of them then?

Only because both were running before I touched anything, and I restarted whatever I had stopped. Neither of us needs both right now.

- **The API on 8600 is required.** It's the backend that holds the data, decisions and jobs, and it also serves the built app.
- **Vite on 5173 is optional.** It only matters while someone is editing the frontend, because it shows code changes instantly. An earlier session most likely started it while working on the frontend and left it running.

If nobody is editing frontend code right now, Vite can be stopped and nothing breaks: the app stays at http://127.0.0.1:8600. If frontend work starts again, `make dev` brings it back. Should I stop it?
i dont get it, api is backend but it runs the frontend to?

Yes. The key point is that the frontend doesn't actually run on a server. It runs in your browser.

`make build` turns the React code into a few plain files: one HTML page, some JavaScript and some CSS, all in `frontend/dist`. A server only has to hand those files to the browser once. After that, the browser runs the app and sends requests back to the server for data.

So the Python server on port 8600 does two jobs:

1. **Hands out the app files.** When you open `http://127.0.0.1:8600/`, it sends back `frontend/dist/index.html` and the JavaScript that comes with it.
2. **Answers data requests.** When the app in your browser asks for `/api/...` (for example the requirements or the audit trail), it returns data from the database.

That's set up in `backend/src/api/routers/static.py`: every `/api/...` path goes to the data endpoints, and any other path gets the built files.

Vite on port 5173 only replaces job 1. Instead of handing out the frozen built files, it compiles `frontend/src` on the fly so your edits appear immediately. It can't do job 2, so it forwards every `/api/...` request to port 8600. That's why the API has to run either way, and Vite is only an extra for frontend development.

```
Normal use:   browser ──► :8600  (app files + data)

Frontend dev: browser ──► :5173  (live app files)
                            └── /api/... ──► :8600  (data)
```

# SharkSight images (D-053). Build context = repo root; .dockerignore is an allowlist (no raw data, data/ or .env).
#   target prod (default): API + built PM app in one container, APP_ENV=production
#   target dev:            API with auto-reload; source is bind-mounted by compose.yaml (profile dev)
# The layout mirrors the repo (/app/backend, /app/frontend, /app/research) so bmw_req.config.ROOT resolves to /app.

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- frontend build
FROM node:22-slim AS web
WORKDIR /app/frontend
COPY frontend/package.json frontend/package-lock.json ./
RUN npm ci
COPY frontend/ ./
RUN npm run build

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- python base
FROM python:3.12-slim AS base
COPY --from=ghcr.io/astral-sh/uv:0.12.5 /uv /usr/local/bin/uv
ENV UV_COMPILE_BYTECODE=1 UV_LINK_MODE=copy UV_PROJECT_ENVIRONMENT=/opt/venv PATH=/opt/venv/bin:$PATH \
    PYTHONUNBUFFERED=1
WORKDIR /app/backend
COPY backend/pyproject.toml backend/uv.lock ./
RUN uv sync --frozen --no-dev --no-install-project
COPY backend/src ./src
COPY backend/scripts ./scripts
RUN uv sync --frozen --no-dev
COPY research/checkpoints/checkpoints.json /app/research/checkpoints/checkpoints.json
# inside the container the server must listen on all interfaces; compose publishes it on the host's 127.0.0.1 only
ENV API_HOST=0.0.0.0 API_PORT=8600 DATA_DIR=/app/data
EXPOSE 8600
HEALTHCHECK --interval=30s --timeout=5s --start-period=20s --retries=3 \
    CMD python -c "import urllib.request; urllib.request.urlopen('http://127.0.0.1:8600/api/state', timeout=4)"
CMD ["python", "-m", "api"]

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- dev: + pytest, reload
FROM base AS dev
RUN uv sync --frozen
ENV APP_ENV=development

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- prod (default)
FROM base AS prod
COPY --from=web /app/frontend/dist /app/frontend/dist
ENV APP_ENV=production

# SharkSight in containers (D-053). Pick a profile:
#   docker compose --profile prod up -d --build   → http://127.0.0.1:8600 (one container, built app)
#   docker compose --profile dev up --build       → http://127.0.0.1:5173 (Vite, live reload) + API on :8600
# Ports are published on 127.0.0.1 only (AGENTS rule 1). data/ (DB, snapshots, 3D models) is mounted, never baked in.

name: sharksight

x-api: &api
  env_file:
    - path: .env
      required: false
  ports:
    - "127.0.0.1:8600:8600"

services:
  app:
    <<: *api
    profiles: [prod]
    build: { context: ., target: prod }
    image: sharksight:prod
    volumes:
      - ./data:/app/data
    restart: unless-stopped

  api-dev:
    <<: *api
    profiles: [dev]
    build: { context: ., target: dev }
    image: sharksight:dev
    environment:
      APP_ENV: development
    volumes:

# Common commands from the repo root. Python runs in backend/ (uv), the PM app in frontend/ (npm).
# Profiles (D-053): development = API auto-reload + Vite dev server; production = API serves the built app.
.PHONY: install api dev build serve test up up-dev down logs

install:  ## Python venv + frontend deps
	cd backend && uv sync
	cd frontend && npm install

# ---- native, development profile
api:  ## API on http://127.0.0.1:8600, auto-reload on backend/src changes
	cd backend && APP_ENV=development uv run python -m api

dev:  ## PM app dev server on http://127.0.0.1:5173 (needs `make api`)
	cd frontend && npm run dev

# ---- native, production profile
build:  ## build frontend/dist
	cd frontend && npm run build

serve: build  ## build, then the API alone serves the app on http://127.0.0.1:8600 (no reload)
	cd backend && APP_ENV=production uv run python -m api

test:  ## Python tests + frontend typecheck
	cd backend && uv run pytest -q
	cd frontend && npm run typecheck

# ---- containers (compose.yaml); stop the native API first: same port, same SQLite file
up:  ## production container on http://127.0.0.1:8600
	docker compose --profile prod up -d --build

up-dev:  ## dev containers: API (reload) on :8600 + Vite on http://127.0.0.1:5173
	docker compose --profile dev up --build

down:  ## stop all containers
	docker compose --profile prod --profile dev down

logs:  ## follow container logs
	docker compose --profile prod --profile dev logs -f

The app now has a development and a production profile, and each runs either directly on your machine or in Docker. I tested all four setups and they work. The production container is running now at http://127.0.0.1:8600.

| | On your machine | In Docker |
|---|---|---|
| **Development**: the server restarts itself when you save Python code, and the app updates live at http://127.0.0.1:5173 | `make api` + `make dev` | `make up-dev` |
| **Production**: one server hands out the built app at http://127.0.0.1:8600 | `make serve` | `make up`, then `make down` to stop and `make logs` to watch |

**How it works**
- **Choosing a profile:** `APP_ENV=development` or `production`. Development is the default, and any other value stops the server at start-up with an error.
- **Server code:** host, port and auto-restart now come from settings instead of being hardcoded in `backend/src/api/main.py`. The defaults are the same as before.
- **Docker:** one `Dockerfile` builds a dev image and a prod image, and `compose.yaml` defines the matching `dev` and `prod` setups.

**Keeping BMW data private (rule 1)**
- `.dockerignore` lists only the files allowed into an image. I scanned the built image: it contains no raw BMW data, no database, no `.env` and no 3D models.
- Containers read `data/` from your disk while running and get the API key from `.env` at start-up.
- The ports are open only on this machine (`127.0.0.1`), not to the network.

**What I tested**
- Production container: reports healthy, and the app, its data and the 3D models all load.
- Development containers: the live app on 5173 reaches the API, and saving a Python file restarted the server.
- The tests are unchanged: 122 pass, and the same 3 `test_api` tests fail as before. The decision is logged as D-053, with README, STATE and tech-stack updated.

**Things to know**
- **Run only one setup at a time.** All of them use port 8600 and the same database file, `data/app.db`.
- **The production container starts again on its own** whenever Docker starts, until you run `make down`.
- **In development, saving a Python file restarts the server**, which also stops any AI job running inside it at that moment, like a wave or an agent-panel run. That wastes money only if a job happens to be running when you save.
- **The data pipeline still runs on your machine, not in Docker.** The containers don't get access to the raw BMW data.

does python code also update itself?

Yes in the development profile, no in production. Python updates a bit differently from the frontend.

**Development (`make api` or `make up-dev`)**
The server watches `backend/src`. When you save a `.py` file it restarts itself, which takes a second or two, and the app's next data request gets the new code. I tested this in the dev container earlier: touching `backend/src/api/labels.py` triggered "Reloading..." and the API came back with 200.

The difference from the frontend:
- **Frontend (Vite):** swaps the changed code into the open browser page. The page keeps its state and you see the change immediately.
- **Python:** restarts the whole server process. The browser page stays open, but anything running inside the server is dropped, which is the caveat about AI jobs mentioned before. You may need to reload the page if a view looks stale.

**Production (`make serve` or `make up`)**
Nothing updates on its own:
- `make serve`: stop it and start it again.
- `make up`: the code is copied into the image when it's built, so run `make up` again to rebuild. That's the case for the container running right now.

**Two other cases**
- **Pipeline commands** (`uv run python -m bmw_req…`) and the scripts in `backend/scripts/` start a fresh process each time, so they always use the latest code.
- **New Python packages** (a change to `pyproject.toml`): auto-reload doesn't install them. Run `uv sync` in `backend/`, or `make up-dev` / `make up` for containers, which rebuild the image.

content.text:
**Database:** it's still SQLite, and it's the same file. The production container doesn't get its own database. It mounts `data/app.db` from your disk, the same file that development and the pipeline commands use. "Production" here only changes how the app runs: no auto-restart, and one server hands out the built app. A decision made in the prod container lands in the same database your dev setup reads.

SQLite itself is fine for this app. It's one server process with one PM at a time, and background jobs run as threads inside that process. Swapping to Postgres or similar would only pay off with several server instances or many simultaneous users, and changing the database would also reverse D-016, which needs the team.

**Can it run on a real production server?** Technically yes, since the image is ready. But three things block it as the code stands:

1. **No login.** The app takes the PM's name from a request header and never checks it (`backend/src/api/deps.py:67`). Anyone who can reach the URL can approve or reject requirements as any name. They can also start AI jobs that spend the $100 OpenAI budget.
2. **Confidential data.** The database holds BMW customer verbatims. Rule 1 says that data goes nowhere except OpenAI, so putting it on a cloud server needs BMW's and the team's approval first.
3. **The server holds state.** It needs exactly one instance and a persistent disk for `data/`, so no auto-scaling and no throwaway containers.

**What I'd suggest instead:**
- **Give production its own database.** A small change: the prod container uses its own folder, e.g. `data-prod/`, seeded from the `demo` snapshot. Then dev experiments can't touch the demo state, and the demo can be reset at any time.
- **If BMW judges need to reach it remotely:** keep it on your laptop, put a login in front of it, and share it through a private tunnel rather than a public server.

"""Budget guard (D-014): reserve worst-case cost before a call, settle with actual usage after.

Thresholds are on total committed spend = settled cost + open reservations.
"""

import logging
import sqlite3

from bmw_req.llm.pricing import (
    CACHE_WRITE_FACTOR,
    FLEX_FACTOR,
    PRICES,
    WEB_SEARCH_CONTENT_TOKENS,
    WEB_SEARCH_PER_CALL,
    Price,
)

log = logging.getLogger(__name__)

WARN_USD = 45.0
BLOCK_NON_DEMO_USD = 70.0
HARD_STOP_USD = 90.0


class BudgetExceeded(RuntimeError):
    pass


def price_for(model: str) -> Price:
    try:
        return PRICES[model]
    except KeyError:
        raise BudgetExceeded(f"No price for model {model!r}; add it to pricing.py before using it") from None


def estimate_tokens(text: str) -> int:
    """Deliberately high input-token estimate: UTF-8 bytes / 2."""
    return len(text.encode("utf-8")) // 2 + 1


def worst_case_usd(model: str, input_tokens: int, max_output_tokens: int = 0, max_tool_calls: int = 0) -> float:
    """List price (no Flex discount, no cache), plus search calls and their content tokens."""
    p = price_for(model)
    tokens_in = input_tokens + max_tool_calls * WEB_SEARCH_CONTENT_TOKENS
    return (tokens_in * p.input + max_output_tokens * p.output) / 1e6 + max_tool_calls * WEB_SEARCH_PER_CALL


def actual_usd(
    model: str,
    *,
    input_tokens: int,
    cached_tokens: int = 0,
    cache_write_tokens: int = 0,
    output_tokens: int = 0,
    search_calls: int = 0,
    flex: bool = False,
) -> float:
    p = price_for(model)
    uncached = max(input_tokens - cached_tokens - cache_write_tokens, 0)
    tokens_usd = (
        uncached * p.input
        + cached_tokens * p.cached_input
        + cache_write_tokens * p.input * CACHE_WRITE_FACTOR
        + output_tokens * p.output
    ) / 1e6
    if flex:
        tokens_usd *= FLEX_FACTOR
    return tokens_usd + search_calls * WEB_SEARCH_PER_CALL


def spent_usd(conn: sqlite3.Connection) -> float:
    return conn.execute("SELECT COALESCE(SUM(cost_usd), 0) FROM llm_usage WHERE status != 'reserved'").fetchone()[0]


def committed_usd(conn: sqlite3.Connection) -> float:
    return conn.execute(
        "SELECT COALESCE(SUM(CASE WHEN status = 'reserved' THEN reserved_usd ELSE cost_usd END), 0) FROM llm_usage"
    ).fetchone()[0]


def reserve(conn: sqlite3.Connection, *, job: str, kind: str, model: str, reserved_usd: float, demo: bool) -> int:
    """Insert a reservation row, or raise BudgetExceeded if it would cross a threshold."""
    conn.execute("BEGIN IMMEDIATE")
    try:
        after = committed_usd(conn) + reserved_usd
        if after > HARD_STOP_USD:
            raise BudgetExceeded(f"Hard stop: ${after:.2f} would exceed ${HARD_STOP_USD:.0f} ({job})")
        if not demo and after > BLOCK_NON_DEMO_USD:
            raise BudgetExceeded(f"Non-demo jobs blocked: ${after:.2f} would exceed ${BLOCK_NON_DEMO_USD:.0f} ({job})")
        cur = conn.execute(
            "INSERT INTO llm_usage (job, demo, kind, model, status, reserved_usd) VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, 'reserved', ?)",
            (job, int(demo), kind, model, reserved_usd),
        )
        conn.execute("COMMIT")
    except BaseException:
        conn.execute("ROLLBACK")
        raise
    if after > WARN_USD:
        log.warning("LLM spend warning: committed $%.2f > $%.0f — re-estimate the plan (D-014)", after, WARN_USD)
    return cur.lastrowid


def settle(conn: sqlite3.Connection, usage_id: int, *, status: str, cost_usd: float, **fields) -> None:
    """Replace a reservation with actual usage. `fields` are llm_usage columns (tokens, response_id, error, ...)."""
    cols = ["status", "cost_usd", *fields]
    sets = ", ".join(f"{c} = ?" for c in cols)
    conn.execute(
        f"UPDATE llm_usage SET {sets}, settled_at = strftime('%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%fZ', 'now') WHERE id = ?",
        (status, cost_usd, *fields.values(), usage_id),
    )

"""In-memory background jobs for the two long, paid pipeline actions: opening a wave and a PM challenge.

One job at a time (both spend OpenAI budget and write a lot). Each job runs in its own thread with its OWN SQLite
connection — the pipeline opens its own anyway — so the shared API connection stays free for reads. Log lines from the
pipeline's return value and from `bmw_req` loggers are captured into the job record.

The pipeline functions are looked up on their modules at call time (`graph.advance`, `challenge.challenge`,
`make_llm`) so tests can monkeypatch them — tests must never trigger a paid call.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import itertools
import logging
import threading
import traceback
from datetime import datetime, timezone
from typing import Any, Callable

_LOCK = threading.Lock()
_JOBS: dict[str, dict] = {}
_IDS = itertools.count(1)
MAX_KEEP = 50


def _now() -> str:
    return datetime.now(timezone.utc).strftime("%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S.%f")[:-3] + "Z"


class _Capture(logging.Handler):
    def __init__(self, job: dict):
        super().__init__(level=logging.INFO)
        self.job = job

    def emit(self, record: logging.LogRecord) -> None:
        try:
            self.job["log"].append(f"{record.levelname.lower()}: {record.getMessage()}")
        except Exception:
            pass


def running() -> dict | None:
    with _LOCK:
        for j in _JOBS.values():
            if j["status"] == "running":
                return {"id": j["id"], "kind": j["kind"]}
    return None


def get(job_id: str) -> dict | None:
    with _LOCK:
        j = _JOBS.get(job_id)
        return None if j is None else {**j, "log": list(j["log"])}


def start(kind: str, fn: Callable[[Callable[[str], None]], Any], meta: dict | None = None) -> str | None:
    """Start `fn(log)` in a background thread. Returns the job id, or None when another job is running."""
    with _LOCK:
        if any(j["status"] == "running" for j in _JOBS.values()):
            return None
        jid = f"{kind}-{next(_IDS)}"
        job = {"id": jid, "kind": kind, "status": "running", "started_at": _now(), "finished_at": None,
               "log": [], "error": None, "result": None, "meta": meta or {}}
        _JOBS[jid] = job
        if len(_JOBS) > MAX_KEEP:
            for old in [k for k, v in _JOBS.items() if v["status"] != "running"][: len(_JOBS) - MAX_KEEP]:
                _JOBS.pop(old, None)

    def log(line: str) -> None:
        job["log"].append(str(line))

    def target() -> None:
        handler = _Capture(job)
        logger = logging.getLogger("bmw_req")
        logger.addHandler(handler)
        prev_level = logger.level
        if logger.level == logging.NOTSET or logger.level > logging.INFO:
            logger.setLevel(logging.INFO)
        try:
            result = fn(log)
            with _LOCK:
                job["result"] = result
                job["status"] = "done"
        except Exception as e:   # surface the failure in the job record
            with _LOCK:
                job["error"] = f"{type(e).__name__}: {e}"
                job["status"] = "error"
            job["log"].append("".join(traceback.format_exception_only(type(e), e)).strip())
        finally:
            logger.removeHandler(handler)
            logger.setLevel(prev_level)
            job["finished_at"] = _now()

    threading.Thread(target=target, name=f"job-{jid}", daemon=True).start()
    return jid


def wait(job_id: str, timeout: float = 10.0) -> dict | None:
    """Test helper: block until the job finishes (or timeout)."""
    import time

    end = time.monotonic() + timeout
    while time.monotonic() < end:
        j = get(job_id)
        if j is None or j["status"] != "running":
            return j
        time.sleep(0.02)
    return get(job_id)


# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ runners
def make_llm(conn):
    """Budget-guarded OpenAI wrapper on the job's own connection (patched in tests)."""
    from bmw_req.llm import LLM

    return LLM(conn=conn)


def run_wave(wave: int, actor: str) -> Callable[[Callable[[str], None]], dict]:
    def fn(log: Callable[[str], None]) -> dict:
        from bmw_req.pipeline import graph

        log(f"opening wave {wave} as {actor} (LLM calls are budget-guarded; replays hit the cache)")
        out = graph.advance(wave, initiated_by=actor)
        for line in out.get("log") or []:
            log(line)
        return {"wave": out.get("wave", wave), "new_requirements": list(out.get("new_requirements") or []),
                "run_id": out.get("run_id")}
    return fn


def run_challenge(req_id: str, question: str, actor: str) -> Callable[[Callable[[str], None]], dict]:
    def fn(log: Callable[[str], None]) -> dict:
        from bmw_req.db import connect
        from bmw_req.pipeline import challenge

        conn = connect()
        try:
            log(f"challenge on {req_id} by {actor}: asking the reasoning model (status → challenged)")
            out = challenge.challenge(conn, make_llm(conn), req_id, question, actor)
            log(f"answered: verdict {(out.get('answer') or {}).get('verdict')}, "
                f"cost ${float(out.get('cost') or 0):.4f}{' (cached)' if out.get('cached') else ''}")
            return out
        finally:
            conn.close()
    return fn

# Claude in Chrome browser automation

You have access to browser automation tools (mcp__claude-in-chrome__*) for interacting with web pages in Chrome. Follow these guidelines for effective browser automation.

## Loading deferred tools

If the mcp__claude-in-chrome__* tools are deferred (must be loaded via ToolSearch before use), load every tool you expect to need in ONE ToolSearch call — the select query accepts a comma-separated list — never one call per tool. Start with the core set:

ToolSearch with query "select:mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_context_mcp,mcp__claude-in-chrome__navigate,mcp__claude-in-chrome__computer,mcp__claude-in-chrome__read_page,mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_create_mcp,mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_close_mcp"

Add task-specific tools to the same call when the task obviously needs them: read_console_messages / read_network_requests for debugging, form_input for forms, gif_creator for recordings, javascript_tool for page scripting.

## GIF recording

When performing multi-step browser interactions that the user may want to review or share, use mcp__claude-in-chrome__gif_creator to record them.

You must ALWAYS:
* Capture extra frames before and after taking actions to ensure smooth playback
* Name the file meaningfully to help the user identify it later (e.g., "login_process.gif")

## Console log debugging

You can use mcp__claude-in-chrome__read_console_messages to read console output. Console output may be verbose. If you are looking for specific log entries, use the 'pattern' parameter with a regex-compatible pattern. This filters results efficiently and avoids overwhelming output. For example, use pattern: "[MyApp]" to filter for application-specific logs rather than reading all console output.

## Alerts and dialogs

IMPORTANT: Do not trigger JavaScript alerts, confirms, prompts, or browser modal dialogs through your actions. These browser dialogs block all further browser events and will prevent the extension from receiving any subsequent commands. Instead, when possible, use console.log for debugging and then use the mcp__claude-in-chrome__read_console_messages tool to read those log messages. If a page has dialog-triggering elements:
1. Avoid clicking buttons or links that may trigger alerts (e.g., "Delete" buttons with confirmation dialogs)
2. If you must interact with such elements, warn the user first that this may interrupt the session
3. Use mcp__claude-in-chrome__javascript_tool to check for and dismiss any existing dialogs before proceeding

If you accidentally trigger a dialog and lose responsiveness, inform the user they need to manually dismiss it in the browser.

## Avoid rabbit holes and loops

When using browser automation tools, stay focused on the specific task. If you encounter any of the following, stop and ask the user for guidance:
- Unexpected complexity or tangential browser exploration
- Browser tool calls failing or returning errors after 2-3 attempts
- No response from the browser extension
- Page elements not responding to clicks or input
- Pages not loading or timing out
- Unable to complete the browser task despite multiple approaches

Explain what you attempted, what went wrong, and ask how the user would like to proceed. Do not keep retrying the same failing browser action or explore unrelated pages without checking in first.

## Tab context and session startup

IMPORTANT: At the start of each browser automation session, call mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_context_mcp first to get information about the user's current browser tabs. Use this context to understand what the user might want to work with before creating new tabs.

Never reuse tab IDs from a previous/other session. Follow these guidelines:
1. Only reuse an existing tab if the user explicitly asks to work with it
2. Otherwise, create a new tab with mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_create_mcp
3. If a tool returns an error indicating the tab doesn't exist or is invalid, call tabs_context_mcp to get fresh tab IDs
4. When a tab is closed by the user or a navigation error occurs, call tabs_context_mcp to see what tabs are available

## Budget guard (as built)

- `bmw_req.llm.LLM.generate()` / `.embed()` are the only way to call OpenAI.
- Each call reserves its worst case in `llm_usage` first (input ≈ UTF-8 bytes ÷ 2, + `max_output_tokens`, + `max_tool_calls` × ($0.01 + 20k content tokens)), at list price. Thresholds apply to settled cost + open reservations.
- After the call, the row is settled with actual tokens (cached, cache-write, reasoning), search calls and cost. Flex is discounted only if the response confirms `service_tier == "flex"`.
- API/connection errors settle at $0; any other failure after the request (e.g. parse error) keeps the worst case.
- A crashed process leaves a `reserved` row that keeps counting — settle or delete it by hand.
- Identical requests (same model, prompt, schema, params) are served from `llm_cache` at $0; pass `use_cache=False` to force a new call.
- The Process → System screen (and `GET /api/budget`) shows spend, committed and the usage log.

## Local machine notes

You can now set the budget and the API key yourself in the app, under **Audit → Usage**. 132 tests pass, including 10 new ones for this. The same 3 old-pipeline tests still fail as before. The rebuilt container is running, and I checked the new section in the browser with your real data. Nothing is committed yet.

**How the limits work**
- **Stop at** (default $90): no AI call is made past this.
- **Ask before spending above** (default $45): past this, every new run has to be confirmed once before it spends. You're at $11.69, so nothing asks yet.
  - When you run a pipeline step in the terminal, it asks `Continue this run? [y/N]`. Answering no stops it before any spending.
  - Setting `BUDGET_CONFIRM=1` confirms a run up front, for unattended runs.
- **The stop is checked first**, so it never asks about a call that would be refused anyway.

**API key**
- A key you save in the app is checked with OpenAI first, using a free call; a rejected key isn't saved.
- It's stored in `data/settings.json`, readable only by your user. It survives snapshot restores and works with the container.
- It takes priority over `.env`. Removing it falls back to `.env`.
- The app never sends the key back; you only ever see `sk-…abcd`.

**Audit:** every change to the key or the limits goes into the audit trail. The key is recorded masked only.

**Rules:** I updated AGENTS rules 12 and 16. The $100 hackathon budget is gone, and agents may not confirm spending or raise a limit on their own; they have to ask you. Logged as D-054, and the hackathon-only "block non-demo jobs at $70" limit is dropped.

**One caveat:** the app has no login, so anyone who can reach port 8600 can change the key and the limits. That's fine while it's only on your machine (`127.0.0.1`), but it has to change before the app is shared.

**Next: code health.** The mapping agent found that the frontend no longer calls any of the old wave-pipeline endpoints, and the 3 failing tests only fail because of stale old-pipeline data. My plan, in order:
1. Remove the dead API routes and their tests. You won't see any difference in the app.
2. Move the helpers the new pipeline still borrows from the old code (audit writer, scoring math, gate prompts) into their new homes.
3. Delete the old pipeline modules.
4. Drop the tables only the old pipeline used. This needs a database migration, so I'll check with you first.

This is the catalogue the "AI agents" page configures. Each agent keeps the defaults its code passes (tier → model,
reasoning effort); the user's overrides live in `app_settings` ("agents") and `LLM.generate()` / `.embed()` apply them on
every call: model, reasoning effort, on/off, and a spend cap (total committed spend of the agent, enforced by the guard).

Jobs of the earlier wave pipeline (D-022 – D-038) match no agent: they stay in the usage log as history and are not
configurable. Order matters — the first pattern that matches a job wins.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import re
from dataclasses import dataclass
from typing import Literal

Kind = Literal["responses", "embeddings"]
Tier = Literal["fast", "smart", "embed"]


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Agent:
    key: str
    name: str
    pipeline: str
    description: str
    pattern: str
    kind: Kind = "responses"
    tier: Tier = "fast"
    effort: str | None = "low"   # the reasoning effort its code passes (None for embeddings)
    web_search: bool = False


PIPELINES = [
    ("sources", "Sources", "Web research and price lists: what goes into the evidence."),
    ("structure", "Structure & context", "Comments → signals → clusters → themes → requirement areas (D-043)."),
    ("definition", "Requirement definition", "Areas → requirements with metrics, target ladders and links (D-048)."),
    ("prioritize", "Prioritization", "The fit gate before the deterministic score (D-050)."),
]

AGENTS: list[Agent] = [
    # sources
    Agent("research_web", "Web research agents", "sources",
          "Search the web for competitor, trend, review and market facts; every item cited with URL and quote.",
          r"^research:(?!findings\b|benchmarks\b)", web_search=True),
    Agent("research_findings", "Research summarizer", "sources",
          "Turns cited web items into findings per car line and market.", r"^research:findings\b"),
    Agent("options_reader", "Price-list reader", "sources",
          "Reads BMW's option price lists (PDF pages) into structured options.", r"^ingest:options\b"),
    # structure & context
    Agent("classify", "Comment classifier", "structure",
          "Every customer comment → signals in the shared aspect space (extract-v4).", r"^classify:extract"),
    Agent("context_mapper", "Context mapper", "structure",
          "Maps study items, options and research onto the same aspects as the comments.",
          r"^classify:(study-aspects|option-aspects|research)\b"),
    Agent("standardize", "Insight writer", "structure",
          "Writes one standardized insight per cluster of signals.", r"^contextualize:standardize\b"),
    Agent("duplicates", "Duplicate checker", "structure",
          "Merges insights that say the same thing.", r"^contextualize:duplicates\b"),
    Agent("themes", "Theme namer", "structure", "Names and describes the themes insights group into.",
          r"^contextualize:themes\b"),
    Agent("evidence_linker", "Evidence linker", "structure",
          "Links themes to study, option and research evidence (supports / contradicts / context).",
          r"^contextualize:link\b"),
    Agent("areas", "Area builder", "structure", "Groups themes into potential requirement areas.", r"^areas\b",
          tier="smart", effort="medium"),
    Agent("elicit", "Requirement drafter (areas)", "structure", "Drafts requirements straight from areas (not run yet).",
          r"^elicit\b", tier="smart", effort="medium"),
    Agent("embed_signals", "Signal embeddings", "structure", "Vectors for clustering the signals.",
          r"^embed:signals:v4\b", kind="embeddings", tier="embed", effort=None),
    Agent("embed_context", "Context embeddings", "structure", "Vectors for insights, themes and evidence nodes (RAG).",
          r"^embed:(nodes|insights|themes)\b", kind="embeddings", tier="embed", effort=None),
    Agent("embed_galaxy", "Comment-map embeddings", "structure", "Vectors that lay out the comments in the 3D view.",
          r"^embed:comments:galaxy\b", kind="embeddings", tier="embed", effort=None),
    # requirement definition
    Agent("benchmark_reader", "Benchmark reader", "definition",
          "Pulls cited spec facts (ranges, charge times, screen sizes …) out of research items.", r"^structure\.benchmarks\b"),
    Agent("benchmark_research", "Benchmark researcher", "definition",
          "Searches the web for missing competitor benchmarks.", r"^research:benchmarks\b", web_search=True),
    Agent("define", "Requirement writer", "definition", "Turns requirement areas into requirements.", r"^define\b",
          tier="smart", effort="medium"),
    Agent("specify", "Target setter", "definition",
          "Gives each requirement a customer metric and a baseline / threshold / target / stretch ladder.", r"^specify\b",
          tier="smart", effort="medium"),
    Agent("couple_recheck", "Link reviewer", "definition", "Re-checks the requirement links the first pass flagged.",
          r"^couple:.*:recheck\b", tier="smart"),
    Agent("couple", "Link finder", "definition", "Finds links between requirements (enables / conflicts / shares).",
          r"^couple\b"),
    # prioritization
    Agent("gate_first", "Fit gate, first pass", "prioritize",
          "Checks brand, segment and market fit of every requirement.", r"^gate:luna\b"),
    Agent("gate_recheck", "Fit gate, re-check", "prioritize",
          "Re-checks the requirements the first pass flagged; its verdict is final.", r"^gate:sol\b", tier="smart"),
]
BY_KEY = {a.key: a for a in AGENTS}
EFFORTS = ("low", "medium", "high")
_COMPILED = [(re.compile(a.pattern), a) for a in AGENTS]


def match(job: str) -> Agent | None:
    """The agent behind a usage-log job name, or None for the earlier wave pipeline."""
    return next((a for rx, a in _COMPILED if rx.search(job)), None)
